scope: Multi-tenant leak via FK paths not BranchScope-protected, raw query surfaces that bypass scopes, FK enforcement bypass via SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0
method: Read-only grep of DB::table / DB::raw / DB::statement / FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS / PRAGMA foreign_keys patterns across app/. Cross-check with BranchScope coverage from Architect specialist.

findings.title: TaxService::destroy() disables FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS to force-delete tax in use
findings.impact: When a tax has no non-deleted items, the code disables FK checks SESSION-WIDE before deleting. ANY subsequent query in the same DB session/connection runs without FK enforcement until the SET=1 line — which is unconditional but a race or exception between line 88 and 89 leaves FK_CHECKS=0 dangling on the connection (Laravel reuses connections). Concurrent requests on the same pooled connection could insert orphan rows. Combined with NF525 audit triggers running on writes, this is a real (if narrow) integrity window.
findings.mitigation_present: Try/catch wraps the block; exceptions surface to controller. But the SET=1 is NOT in a finally{} — exception between SET=0 and the next SET=1 leaves connection in dangerous state.
findings.recommendation: Wrap in try/finally: `try { DB::statement('SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0'); $tax->delete(); } finally { DB::statement('SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=1'); }`. Or refactor: cascade-delete tax_items rows explicitly via a DB::transaction, avoiding the FK-disable hack entirely.

findings.title: ItemCategoryService::destroy() also disables FK checks (PRAGMA on SQLite, SET on MySQL)
findings.impact: Same shape as SEC-001 but cross-driver. PRAGMA foreign_keys=0 on SQLite is the same hazard; on a long-running SQLite test session, this stays at 0 until re-enabled. SQLite PRAGMA setting is per-connection, so test isolation can leak. MySQL: same as SEC-001. Code IS wrapped in DB::transaction (line 169) so the SET-OFF block is at least atomic — but no try/finally so an exception still leaves FK_CHECKS=0 until the next query in the closure errors out.
findings.mitigation_present: DB::transaction provides rollback for the delete itself.
findings.recommendation: Same as SEC-001: try/finally around the FK-disable. Long-term: explicit cascade in the closure, drop the FK-disable pattern entirely. Mirror the pattern from BranchScope::class — explicit and auditable beats clever and short.

findings.title: DB::table() bypasses BranchScope in 30+ service/controller call sites — verified no current exploitable leak, but pattern is fragile
findings.evidence_path: AvailabilityService:296,305,321,630,671,707,713 + ZReportService:651 + OrderService:2562 + FrontendOrderService:853,975 + LoyaltyController:218,223,305,483,513 + LoyaltyService:56 + PosRedemptionService:155 + LoyaltyQrSigner:143 + Observability/SyncOverviewController:76,128,308,329,336,427,443,464,500,513
findings.impact: `DB::table()` COMPLETELY BYPASSES Eloquent global scopes including BranchScope. Each call site MUST manually add tenant scoping. VERIFIED CALL SITES (sample of 5 high-risk): (1) AvailabilityService:296-298 → explicit `->where('branch_id', $branchId)` — SAFE. (2) LoyaltyController:484 → `->where('user_id', $user->id)` from authenticated $request->user() — SAFE (user-scoped is tighter than branch-scoped for loyalty data). (3) LoyaltyController:513 → same user_id filter from authenticated user — SAFE for same reason. (4) ZReportService:651 → order_items joined via order_id from already-scoped Order context — depends on caller passing branch-correct order. (5) Observability/SyncOverviewController — admin-only routes per route group middleware — SAFE for current scope. CONCLUSION: no confirmed exploitable cross-tenant leak found at audit time. P1 retained because the pattern is fragile (next engineer adds DB::table without filter), not because of confirmed exploit.
findings.mitigation_present: Each verified call site uses user_id (authenticated context) or explicit branch_id filter. Admin-only routes are middleware-gated.
findings.recommendation: Downgraded from P0 → P1 after verification. Still requires: (1) Audit remaining ~25 unverified DB::table call sites systematically. (2) Add a static-analysis rule (PHPStan custom rule or ripgrep CI check) that flags `DB::table('<branch-scoped-table>')` without nearby `branch_id` reference. (3) For session-scoped queries, prefer `Eloquent\Model::query()` over `DB::table()` — Eloquent applies BranchScope automatically. Tables to flag in CI: orders, order_items, order_payments, cash_movements, cash_drawer_sessions, stock_movements, stock_levels, item_branch_availability, push_notifications, printers, dining_tables, pos_parked_orders, pending_payment_confirmations, webhook_events. (Note: loyalty_transactions intentionally not branch-scoped — user-centric.)

findings.title: DB::raw() in UPDATE expressions (AvailabilityService:310-313, ZReportCashEnrichmentService:170-172, PosReceiptPrintController:47, PosCategoryController:92,98) — SQL fragment construction
findings.evidence_excerpt:
DB::raw(
    "CASE WHEN daily_consumed_qty + {$qty} > max_daily_qty "
    . "THEN max_daily_qty ELSE daily_consumed_qty + {$qty} END"
)
findings.impact: `{$qty}` is interpolated directly into raw SQL. The variable comes from `(int) $line->quantity` (line 294), so a (int) cast is the guard — safe AS-IS because PHP's int cast strips any string to 0-or-number. ZReportCashEnrichmentService uses an enum value (PosPaymentMethod::CASH which is an int constant) — also safe. But the pattern is fragile: future engineers may interpolate non-cast values.
findings.mitigation_present: All current call sites cast or use enum int constants — no user input reaches the raw SQL.
findings.recommendation: Add a code review checklist entry: "any DB::raw with string interpolation must demonstrate the interpolated value is type-cast or enum-bound". Or refactor AvailabilityService:310-313 to use parameter binding via DB::raw("CASE WHEN daily_consumed_qty + ? > max_daily_qty THEN max_daily_qty ELSE daily_consumed_qty + ? END") + ->whereRaw bindings.

findings.title: BranchScope short-circuits when !App::runningInConsole() === false AND !App::runningUnitTests()
findings.impact: Console commands (artisan ...) run WITHOUT BranchScope unless inside unit tests. This is correct for cron commands (FiscalSequenceRetry, OutboxRetry etc.) which legitimately need cross-branch access. BUT any artisan command that takes a user-id argument and queries scoped models will return CROSS-TENANT data. Example: a hypothetical `artisan order:cancel --user=X --order=Y` could pull an order from a different branch than the user's branch if the command developer assumed BranchScope was active.
findings.mitigation_present: Most artisan commands are admin-only (run via deploy or owner). Cron commands deliberately need cross-branch.
findings.recommendation: Document loudly in BranchScope.php docblock: "Console (artisan) bypasses this scope. Commands handling user-scoped data MUST manually scope or call User::withGlobalScope(BranchScope::class)". Add a static analysis or test that lints command classes against direct Eloquent calls without explicit branch_id.

findings.title: Loyalty manual_add via admin POST inserts raw DB::table('loyalty_transactions') — bypasses model events + audit trail
findings.impact: Inserting directly via DB::table bypasses any LoyaltyTransaction model events (`creating`, `created`) and any future BranchScope (loyalty_transactions does not currently have BranchScope but might gain one). Audit log writer for loyalty events likely depends on model events. Inconsistent with PosRedemptionService which uses Eloquent.
findings.mitigation_present: Admin role permission gate at controller layer; UNIQUE(user_id, order_id, type) DB constraint catches obvious replays.
findings.recommendation: Refactor to `LoyaltyTransaction::create([...])`. Same DB rows but goes through Eloquent → events → audit log writers. 5-LOC change.

findings.title: WizardProfileBranchScope (NEW 2026-05-18) — correctly implements OR-NULL for global profiles
findings.impact: Custom scope for item_wizard_profiles.branch_id_scope (nullable). Sound implementation: nullable means "published globally". Mirrors BranchScope structure including the User-recursion guard. Sister test referenced.

findings.title: withoutGlobalScope(BranchScope::class) used in 8+ Frontend controllers — by design, but each is a manual-audit checkpoint
findings.impact: Each bypass is intentional (kiosk pre-auth lookup, payment reconciliation across branches, guest user phone lookup). Pattern is documented in code comments. Risk: a future engineer adds a new withoutGlobalScope call without realizing it disables tenant isolation.
findings.mitigation_present: Code comments explain rationale at each call site.
findings.recommendation: Document a code-review rule: "any new withoutGlobalScope(BranchScope::class) requires explanatory comment + sister test + security-team approval". Add a sentinel test that counts bypass sites and fails when an undocumented one appears (foreshadowing P0 catch via grep+count CI gate).

findings.title: FreshOrderSeed::handle() SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0 + TRUNCATE — see DBA-005, classified as security/data-loss as well
findings.impact: Duplicate finding with DBA-005. Listed here for completeness from security angle: TRUNCATE bypasses ALL triggers including NF525 fiscal immutability triggers on stock_movements (if extended) and audit_logs (if extended in the cleanup pattern). Currently scoped to orders/order_items so direct NF525 impact = nil, BUT pattern propagation is the threat.

summary.highest_impact_finding: SEC-001 + SEC-002 (FK disable pattern in destroy() services without try/finally — session-wide leak if exception fires between SET=0 and SET=1)
summary.next_class_of_finding: SEC-003 verified — no confirmed exploitable cross-tenant leak from DB::table() bypass; pattern fragility remains. CI grep gate recommended.
